identity.name: Lecithins
identity.chemical_class: Complex phospholipid/phosphatide mixture (mainly phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylinositol)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic phospholipids reduce oil-water interfacial tension and stabilize dispersed phases.
common_food_categories: infant formula and foods for special medical purposes

adi.basis: EFSA concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI for lecithins (E322).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation and follow-up concluded no safety concern at reported/refined uses, including infants below 16 weeks up to MPL in relevant formula categories.

concerns.summary: A 2025 randomized trial including soy lecithin reported changes in microbiome-related metabolites (e.g., reduced short-chain fatty acids) under emulsifier supplementation, without clear inflammation/metabolic harm over the intervention period.
Soy-lecithin sensitivity can occur in some soy-allergic individuals, but pediatric randomized crossover data suggested most children with non-IgE-mediated soy allergy tolerated soy lecithin.

Mechanistic literature links phosphatidylcholine metabolism by gut microbiota to TMAO-associated cardiovascular risk signals, but this has not translated into EFSA/FDA/JECFA restriction of E322 at authorized uses.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA (2017) found no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at refined exposures for the general population >1 year.
EFSA (2020) found no safety concern for infant formula/FSMP uses up to MPL for infants below 16 weeks.
JECFA set ADI to NOT LIMITED.
21 CFR 184.1400 affirms lecithin as GRAS under cGMP conditions of use.

adi_exceedance.notes: Classical ADI exceedance is not applicable because EFSA set no numerical ADI and JECFA ADI is not limited; EFSA still identified higher exposure estimates in some child/infant scenarios but concluded no safety concern at evaluated uses.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus across EFSA, FDA, and JECFA supports safety at permitted uses, but minor unresolved mechanistic and subgroup-specific concerns (microbiome/TMAO/allergenicity edge cases) argue against classifying as fully risk_free.
key_factors: EFSA no numerical ADI and no safety concern at refined exposure
EFSA 2020 infant follow-up found no concern up to MPL
FDA GRAS status in 21 CFR 184.1400 with cGMP condition
Some mechanistic and subgroup-level concerns remain but are not strong enough for moderate/high tier
